s1.syndrome_frame: A chronic skin condition characterized by asymptomatic red to brown macules and papules with a symmetric distribution on the trunk and extremities, accompanied by systemic findings including hypereosinophilia and elevated tryptase levels
salient_findings: Red to brown macules and papules on trunk and extremities
key_facts: Male patient in his 20s
12-month history of skin lesions
Lesions initially appeared on trunk and spread to upper and proximal lower extremities
Lesions were symmetrically distributed and did not coalesce
Face, distal extremities, and mucous membranes were unaffected
Some lesions resolved spontaneously with residual hyperpigmentation
Blood cell count showed hypereosinophilia
Elevated tryptase levels
Elevated vitamin B12 levels
Negative serologic tests for HIV, hepatitis A, B, and C
Negative tests for parasitic infections
Skin biopsy showed nodular infiltration of histiocytes with lymphocytes and eosinophils
Bone marrow analysis showed hypercellularity with myeloid hyperplasia and increased eosinophils

raw.syndrome_frame: A chronic skin condition characterized by asymptomatic red to brown macules and papules with a symmetric distribution on the trunk and extremities, accompanied by systemic findings including hypereosinophilia and elevated tryptase levels
salient_findings: Red to brown macules and papules on trunk and extremities
key_facts: Male patient in his 20s
12-month history of skin lesions
Lesions initially appeared on trunk and spread to upper and proximal lower extremities
Lesions were symmetrically distributed and did not coalesce
Face, distal extremities, and mucous membranes were unaffected
Some lesions resolved spontaneously with residual hyperpigmentation
Blood cell count showed hypereosinophilia
Elevated tryptase levels
Elevated vitamin B12 levels
Negative serologic tests for HIV, hepatitis A, B, and C
Negative tests for parasitic infections
Skin biopsy showed nodular infiltration of histiocytes with lymphocytes and eosinophils
Bone marrow analysis showed hypercellularity with myeloid hyperplasia and increased eosinophils

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of skin lesions, hypereosinophilia, elevated tryptase levels, and elevated vitamin B12 levels, along with the bone marrow analysis showing hypercellularity with myeloid hyperplasia and increased eosinophils, and the presence of the FIP1L1-PDGFRA fusion gene, are all consistent with systemic mastocytosis.

rejected.label: generalized eruptive histiocytosis
rejected.why: The skin biopsy showed nodular infiltration of histiocytes, but the presence of hypereosinophilia, elevated tryptase, and the FIP1L1-PDGFRA fusion gene point more towards systemic mastocytosis.

rejected.label: eruption
rejected.why: Too non-specific and does not account for the systemic findings such as hypereosinophilia and elevated tryptase levels.

rejected.label: skin eruption
rejected.why: Similar to 'eruption', it is too non-specific and does not explain the systemic findings or the specific laboratory results.

rejected.label: benign cephalic histiocytosis
rejected.why: The condition typically presents in early childhood, and the patient's age and the presence of systemic symptoms do not align with this diagnosis.
